name: Lucky Strike Entertainment
desc: Operates bowling centres and entertainment venues in North America under the Lucky Strike, Bowlero and AMF brands.
markets: Consumers and corporate groups across the United States, with venues also in Canada and Mexico; no known expansion beyond North America.
rationale: Consumer venue brand with corporate-event business could use F1 for hospitality, guest experiences and US sports-media visibility, though footprint is North American only.
changed: Renamed from Bowlero Corporation in 2024

name: Quad
desc: Provides marketing services including commercial print, in-store signage, direct mail, creative and digital media for retailers, consumer brands and publishers.
markets: Large brand and retailer clients, mainly in the United States, with operations also in Latin America and Europe.
rationale: B2B marketing firm with little consumer awareness; F1 could serve client hospitality and showcase large-format print and activation work, but fit is modest.
changed: Renamed from Quad/Graphics

name: Trump Media & Technology Group
desc: Owns the Truth Social platform, Truth+ streaming and the Truth.Fi financial brand, serving mainly United States users.
markets: Users and advertisers almost entirely in the United States; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Polarising political brand with a US-only audience and small revenue; limited appeal for mainstream F1 partnership or brand-safety conscious teams.
changed: Listed on Nasdaq in 2024 through a SPAC merger with Digital World Acquisition Corp

name: Turk Telekom
desc: Provides fixed and mobile broadband, voice, television and digital services to consumers and enterprises in Turkey.
markets: Customers in Turkey only; large local brand with a history of sports sponsorship and no verified expansion abroad.
rationale: Household-name Turkish operator with sports-sponsorship experience could use F1 for brand marketing and enterprise hospitality, though customers are all domestic.
changed: Turkey Wealth Fund became controlling shareholder in 2022

name: du
desc: Provides mobile, home broadband, television and enterprise connectivity services in the United Arab Emirates.
markets: Consumers and businesses in the UAE; no known operations outside the country.
rationale: Major Gulf operator with strong brand marketing, enterprise clients for hospitality and proximity to the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, though audience is domestic.

name: Merlin Entertainments
desc: Operates visitor attractions including Legoland parks, Madame Tussauds, Sea Life aquariums, the London Eye and Alton Towers.
markets: Visitors across Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific at 140-plus attractions in about 25 countries; continues to open new sites.
rationale: Family leisure brand with worldwide footprint could use F1 for cross-promotion, guest experiences and Legoland brand tie-ins with the LEGO partnership.
changed: Taken private in 2019 by a consortium of Blackstone, KIRKBI and CPP Investments
f1: Legoland parks use the LEGO brand; LEGO is a current F1 partner and its owner KIRKBI is a Merlin shareholder

name: Sea Limited
desc: Owns the Shopee e-commerce platform, Garena games including Free Fire and the SeaMoney financial services arm.
markets: Consumers in Southeast Asia, Taiwan and Brazil through Shopee, Garena and SeaMoney.
rationale: Large consumer internet brand with Southeast Asian and Latin American reach could use F1 for brand marketing and Garena gaming activations.

name: Hipgnosis Songs Fund
desc: Was a London-listed investment trust owning royalty rights in song catalogues of well-known artists, managed by Hipgnosis Song Management.
markets: Held music catalogues earning royalties worldwide; no longer an independent listed vehicle after the takeover.
rationale: Asset-owning fund vehicle with no consumer brand or marketing activity; no practical F1 partnership case.
changed: Taken over by Concord and delisted in 2024

name: Cutting Edge Media Music
desc: London company providing music production and licensing services for advertising, film and television, according to Crunchbase.
markets: Clients not stated in the data; presumed to serve media producers from London.
rationale: Little is known about this small business; brand marketing needs and international ambitions are unclear, so F1 fit is weak.

name: ONE Championship
desc: Promotes mixed martial arts, Muay Thai and kickboxing events across Asia, earning revenue from broadcast rights, sponsorship and ticketing.
markets: Live events across Asia with broadcast distribution worldwide, including the United States.
rationale: Asia-focused sports property with global broadcast and sponsor base could pursue cross-promotion with F1 in Asian markets and shared fan audiences.

name: New Pluto Global
desc: Described by Crunchbase as a creative-driven site for storytellers and content creators in the creator economy.
markets: Markets not stated in the data; presumed United States only.
rationale: Unrecognised company with unclear customers or scale; no evidence of brand-marketing capacity for an F1 partnership.

name: TelevisaUnivision
desc: Spanish-language media company operating Univision and Televisa networks, streaming service ViX and digital audio across the United States and Mexico.
markets: Spanish-speaking audiences in the United States, Mexico and Latin America; ViX streaming extends to further markets.
rationale: Reaches Hispanic audiences in the US and Mexico, both growing F1 markets, so broadcast and advertising tie-ins with race events are plausible.
changed: Formed in 2022 by merging Televisa's content assets with Univision

name: Univision Communications
desc: Operates Spanish-language Univision and UniMas television networks, local stations and digital audio for Hispanic audiences in the United States.
markets: Hispanic audiences in the United States; now part of TelevisaUnivision with Mexican content links.
rationale: Large US Hispanic audience with advertising and event tie-ins, but now merged into TelevisaUnivision so engagement would run through that group.
changed: Merged with Televisa's media assets in 2022 to form TelevisaUnivision

name: AMC Networks
desc: Owns the AMC, WE tv, IFC and Sundance TV channels, streaming services Acorn TV and Shudder, and a production studio.
markets: Subscribers mainly in the United States, with channels and streaming services also sold in Europe and Latin America.
rationale: Content and streaming brand with sports-adjacent programming could use F1 for audience promotion, but is mainly a US cable operator.

name: Newsmax Media
desc: Operates the Newsmax cable news channel, newsmax.com, a magazine and streaming services for a conservative-leaning United States audience.
markets: Audience almost entirely in the United States; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Politically positioned US news brand with a domestic audience; limited fit with F1's global, brand-neutral partner base.

name: Relativity Media
desc: Film and television studio founded in 2004 that financed and distributed films and ran a sports unit.
markets: Hollywood production and distribution; current operating scale and owners after repeated bankruptcies are not confirmed.
rationale: Brand has been through two bankruptcies with unclear current operations; weak and uncertain case for an F1 partnership.
changed: Filed for Chapter 11 in 2015 and again in 2018

name: Sinclair, Inc.
desc: Owns or operates about 185 local television stations across 80-plus United States markets and the Tennis Channel.
markets: Local stations and advertisers in the United States only; no international operations.
rationale: Local broadcaster with a regional US advertiser base and sports content; partnership value limited to domestic advertising and hospitality.
changed: Renamed from Sinclair Broadcast Group

name: Angel Studios
desc: Film studio and streaming service that releases member-funded family-oriented titles such as The Chosen and Sound of Freedom.
markets: Audiences and members mainly in the United States; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Values-driven family brand with a US member base; F1 offers little audience overlap beyond general reach.

name: Seeker Music
desc: Described by Crunchbase as a music company offering artist services and catalogue investments, based in Los Angeles.
markets: Markets not stated in the data; presumed United States only.
rationale: Unrecognised business with unclear roster and ownership; no basis to judge brand marketing needs, so F1 fit is weak.

name: OTE Group
desc: Provides mobile, fixed-line, broadband and television services in Greece through the Cosmote brand.
markets: Consumers and businesses in Greece; no verified operations in other countries.
rationale: Established Greek operator with strong sports-rights presence and a Deutsche Telekom parent, though customers are domestic only.
f1: Parent Deutsche Telekom owns T-Mobile, a current F1 partner

name: Canal+
desc: Runs pay-television channels, streaming services and the StudioCanal film production and distribution arm for subscribers in France, Africa and Europe.
markets: Subscribers in France, Africa, Europe and Asia, expanded by the 2025 MultiChoice acquisition.
rationale: Pay-TV group already broadcasting F1 in France gives it a direct audience-marketing and hospitality interest across its European and African markets.
changed: Separated from Vivendi and listed in London in 2024; acquired MultiChoice in 2025
f1: Broadcast rights holder for Formula 1 in France

name: ODEON Cinemas Group
desc: Operates ODEON and UCI cinemas across the United Kingdom, Ireland, Spain, Italy, Germany, Austria and other European countries.
markets: Cinema-goers across the United Kingdom, Ireland and continental Europe; no known expansion outside Europe.
rationale: Consumer venue network could host F1 screenings and cross-promotions, but it is a mid-marketing-budget European chain owned by AMC.
changed: Acquired by AMC Entertainment in 2016

name: Beast Industries
desc: Media and consumer company of YouTuber MrBeast, producing video content and owning the Feastables snacks and chocolate brand.
markets: Global YouTube audience and Feastables products sold at retailers in the United States and other countries.
rationale: Young global audience and consumer products make F1 content collaboration and product activation plausible, though not an established sports sponsor.

name: Playtika
desc: Develops and publishes free-to-play mobile games including Slotomania, Bingo Blitz, House of Fun and Caesars Slots.
markets: Players across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; revenue from in-app purchases and advertising.
rationale: Global mobile-game publisher with large marketing budgets could use F1 for user acquisition and brand building among US and European players.
f1: Caesars Slots game licensed from Caesars Entertainment, a current F1 partner

name: Downtown Music Holdings
desc: Music publishing and services group whose businesses include Downtown Music Publishing, Songtrust, FUGA digital distribution and CD Baby.
markets: Independent artists, labels and publishers worldwide through distribution and rights services.
rationale: B2B music services with little consumer brand; F1 relevance limited to music-rights tie-ins and artist events.
changed: Universal Music Group agreed to acquire it in 2025; completion not confirmed

name: Recognition Music Group
desc: Described by Crunchbase as an audio recording and production company, apparently a music rights investment and management business.
markets: Markets not stated in the data; presumed United Kingdom based.
rationale: Unrecognised company with unclear assets and ownership; no evidence of consumer marketing, so F1 fit is weak.

name: fuboTV
desc: Provides a sports-focused live television streaming service with channels, news and on-demand content for subscribers in North America.
markets: Subscribers in the United States and Canada; no confirmed wider expansion.
rationale: Sports-led streamer seeks subscriber growth and could use F1 audience tie-ins, but its North American-only reach limits global value.
changed: Combined with Hulu + Live TV in 2025, with Disney taking a majority stake

name: Alliance Entertainment
desc: Wholesale distributor and retailer of music, movies, video games, electronics and collectibles supplying retailers across the United States.
markets: Retail and wholesale customers in the United States; no verified international operations.
rationale: Wholesale distributor with limited consumer brand; F1 licensed merchandise distribution is conceivable, but brand-marketing fit is weak.

name: Atmosphere
desc: Provides an ad-supported streaming television platform for businesses, showing free content on screens in bars, restaurants, gyms and offices.
markets: Venues in the United States; no verified operations abroad.
rationale: Venue-screen network could carry F1 content to bars and restaurants, but it is a domestic ad-supported platform.

name: Cirque du Soleil
desc: Produces touring and resident live acrobatic shows such as O, Mystere and Kooza, including in Las Vegas, for ticket-buying audiences.
markets: Audiences across North America, Europe and Asia through resident and touring shows; Las Vegas is a major base.
rationale: Global live-entertainment brand with a major Las Vegas presence suits F1 hospitality, event entertainment and guest-experience tie-ins around Grand Prix weekends.
changed: Restructured under creditor protection in 2020

name: Kodak
desc: Sells commercial printing equipment and plates, packaging, advanced chemicals, and film and photography products.
markets: Business customers worldwide in printing and packaging, plus film products sold to photographers and film makers.
rationale: Heritage imaging brand with global B2B reach could use F1 for brand visibility and a technology showcase, though marketing budget is modest.
changed: Emerged from Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2013

name: Ooredoo
desc: Provides mobile, fixed, broadband and enterprise telecommunications services across the Middle East, North Africa and Southeast Asia.
markets: Operations in Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, Iraq, Algeria, Tunisia, Maldives and Indonesia, serving consumers and enterprises.
rationale: Qatar-based operator with brand marketing and multi-country presence suits F1 hospitality, connectivity showcase and Qatar Grand Prix activation.

name: NEP Group
desc: Provides outsourced television production, sports broadcast trucks, remote production, studios and live event services to broadcasters and sports rights holders.
markets: Broadcast and live-event customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific, serving major sports events.
rationale: B2B broadcast services provider with major sports clients could use F1 to showcase production technology, though it has limited consumer marketing.

name: FC Barcelona
desc: Spanish professional football club playing in La Liga, earning revenue from matchdays, broadcasting, commercial deals and merchandising.
markets: Fans and commercial partners worldwide, with matches in Barcelona and overseas tours and licensing.
rationale: One of the world's most followed sports brands, with global partner programme; shared Barcelona venues and fan bases suggest hospitality and content cross-promotion.

name: Sanrio
desc: Character company behind Hello Kitty, My Melody, Kuromi and Cinnamoroll, earning from licensing, merchandise, retail stores and theme parks.
markets: Licensed products and stores in Japan, North America, Europe and the rest of Asia.
rationale: Global character brand with licensing culture suits collaborative merchandise and family-fan campaigns around F1 events, though not an obvious sports advertiser.

name: Tving
desc: Offers a South Korean streaming service with live television, original series and sports rights such as Korean baseball.
markets: Subscribers in South Korea; no verified international operations.
rationale: Domestic streamer with a sports-rights focus, but audience and marketing reach are confined to Korea.
changed: Spun off from CJ ENM as a standalone company in 2020

name: Blacknut
desc: Operates a subscription cloud gaming service streaming games to televisions, phones and computers, with distribution partnerships.
markets: Subscribers in Europe and North America through partnerships with device makers and telecom operators.
rationale: Cloud gaming brand could pair F1 content with gaming audiences, but it is a small subscription service with limited budget.

name: Matchroom
desc: Promotes boxing, darts, snooker and pool events, including Anthony Joshua and Katie Taylor fights, with global broadcast partners.
markets: Events in the United Kingdom, United States and Saudi Arabia, broadcast worldwide.
rationale: Event promoter with big-ticket hospitality and sponsorship sales could share corporate guests and fan audiences with F1 in Britain and the Gulf.

name: National Football League
desc: Runs the top United States professional American football league of 32 teams, earning from media rights, sponsorship and licensing.
markets: Fans mainly in the United States, with international games in Europe and Latin America and global media distribution.
rationale: Major sports property with US dominance and growing international games; cross-promotion with F1 in Las Vegas and Miami is possible, though it rarely buys sponsorship.

name: Overtime
desc: Makes short-form sports content and runs leagues such as Overtime Elite and OT7 for Gen Z fans across social platforms.
markets: Audiences mainly in the United States via social media; no verified overseas expansion.
rationale: Gen Z sports media brand could extend F1 youth reach through content partnership, though sponsorship budget and scale are limited.

name: League One Volleyball
desc: United States women's professional volleyball league with teams in several cities, earning from tickets, media and sponsorship.
markets: Teams and fans in United States cities only; no verified international plans.
rationale: Young US league with sponsor-led revenue; F1 offers little audience fit for a domestic women's sports property.

name: Kuku FM
desc: Audio entertainment app offering audiobooks, podcasts, audio series and short audio courses in Hindi and regional Indian languages.
markets: Listeners in India across Hindi and regional-language markets; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Indian consumer app with growing subscribers could use India-focused F1 content tie-ins, but marketing scale is modest and domestic.

name: Millicom (Tigo)
desc: Provides mobile, cable television and broadband services under the Tigo brand across Latin America including Colombia, Guatemala, Paraguay and Bolivia.
industry: Latin American telecom and cable operator
markets: Consumers and businesses across Colombia, Central America, Paraguay and Bolivia; Latin American focus.
rationale: Latin American operator with consumer brand marketing could use F1 interest in Mexico and Brazil for hospitality and customer promotion.

name: OnlyFans
desc: Operates a subscription platform where creators, mostly adult content creators, sell photos, videos and live streams directly to fans.
markets: Creators and subscribers worldwide, with the largest audiences in the United States and United Kingdom.
rationale: Adult-content positioning makes sponsorship with a family-brand sport very unlikely and effectively restricted.

name: Pearson
desc: Sells digital learning, assessments, qualifications such as Edexcel, English language tests, and textbooks to schools, universities and employers.
markets: Learners and institutions across the United Kingdom, United States, India, China and other markets.
rationale: Global education brand could use F1 for STEM, skills and sponsorship tie-ins with educational content and B2B hospitality.

name: Valencia CF
desc: Spanish professional football club playing in La Liga at the Mestalla stadium, earning from matchdays, broadcasting and commercial deals.
markets: Fans and commercial partners mainly in Spain; operations based in Valencia.
rationale: La Liga club with modest commercial income; shares only a Spanish market focus with F1 and has limited partnership budget.

name: LeEco
desc: Chinese internet and consumer electronics group, formerly Letv, known for streaming video, smart televisions, smartphones and electric vehicles.
markets: Primarily China, with a short-lived attempt to enter the United States and India.
rationale: Group suffered a funding crisis from 2017 and its current operating status is unclear, so a partnership is unrealistic.
changed: Financial collapse from 2017 after rapid expansion

name: K Wave Media
desc: Described by Crunchbase as a media and entertainment company developing content and franchises tied to the Korean wave.
markets: Markets not stated in the data; content aimed at fans of Korean culture.
rationale: Unrecognised company with unclear ownership and scale; no verified marketing capacity for an F1 partnership.

name: Scopely
desc: Develops and publishes mobile games including Monopoly Go!, Marvel Strike Force, Star Trek Fleet Command and Stumble Guys.
markets: Players across North America, Europe and Asia; hundreds of millions of downloads.
rationale: Global mobile-game publisher with heavy marketing spend could use F1 for user acquisition and in-game brand activations.
parent: Savvy Games Group (Public Investment Fund, Saudi Arabia)
changed: Acquired by Savvy Games Group in 2023

name: Deezer
desc: Offers a music streaming service with over 120 million tracks, personalised recommendations and podcasts in about 180 countries.
markets: Subscribers across Europe, Latin America and other regions, with the strongest base in France.
rationale: Music streamer with consumer marketing could use F1 for playlist and content partnerships, though its scale is smaller than the largest rivals.

name: Cinq Music
desc: Record label and music distribution company providing label services, distribution and rights management for independent artists and labels.
markets: Independent artists and labels, presumed mainly in the United States; wider reach not confirmed.
rationale: Small music services company with limited brand awareness; F1 offers little direct fit.

name: Go Digital Music
desc: Described by Crunchbase as a media and technology holding company focused on digital media and entertainment.
markets: Markets not stated in the data; presumed United States only.
rationale: Unrecognised holding company with unclear products and scale; no evidence of brand marketing needs for an F1 partnership.

name: IMAX
desc: Develops IMAX giant-screen cinema systems and sells projection and sound technology to theatres worldwide.
markets: Theatres across North America, Europe and Asia, with China a large market.
rationale: Premium-screen brand with global theatre network suits technology showcase and fan-experience content; F1 content already draws cinema audiences.

name: Primary Wave
desc: Music publisher and brand management company that buys interests in artists' catalogues and licenses them for advertising and film.
markets: Catalogue licensing with advertisers and studios, presumed mainly in the United States.
rationale: Catalogue owner could license songs for F1 content, but it is a B2B rights business with little consumer marketing.

name: The North Road Company
desc: Multi-genre film and television studio that develops and produces scripted films and series for streamers, networks and distributors.
markets: Customers are streamers and distributors; presumed United States based.
rationale: B2B content producer with little public brand awareness; F1 relevance limited to possible motorsport content collaboration.

name: Rumble
desc: Operates a video sharing platform positioned as an alternative to YouTube, with creators, advertising, subscriptions and a cloud services business.
markets: Creators and viewers mainly in the United States and Canada, with a global audience online.
rationale: Video platform with creator audiences could host F1 content, but its political positioning and mixed brand safety limit mainstream sponsor appeal.

name: WildBrain
desc: Creates and distributes children's content such as Peanuts, Teletubbies and Strawberry Shortcake and runs the WildBrain Spark YouTube network.
markets: Content and licensed brands reaching families across North America, Europe and Asia via television, streaming and YouTube.
rationale: Children's entertainment brand owner with licensing culture; weak F1 audience fit apart from family merchandise or content collaborations.

name: Azerion
desc: Provides advertising technology, casual games and publisher services to brands from the Netherlands.
industry: digital advertising and casual games platform
markets: Advertisers and publishers across Europe and the United States.
rationale: Digital ad and games platform with brand clients; F1 could support advertising-platform showcases, though it is mainly B2B.

name: Truecaller
desc: Mobile app that identifies unknown callers, blocks spam and fraud calls, and offers caller ID, call recording and some payments.
markets: Users worldwide with India as its largest market, plus Europe, Middle East and Africa.
rationale: Consumer app with large Indian user base and sponsorship history could use F1 for brand awareness in India and emerging markets.

name: GIBO Holdings
desc: Describes itself as an AI-driven animation platform producing and distributing anime-style and other animated content through streaming services.
markets: Audience and operations centred on Malaysia and Southeast Asia; wider markets not confirmed.
rationale: Small listed company with limited consumer awareness and volatile finances; weak case for an F1 partnership.

name: Datacentrex (formerly Thumzup Media)
desc: Began as a mobile app paying people to post about brands on social media and has pivoted toward digital assets.
industry: social advertising app turned digital assets firm
markets: Users and advertisers presumed mainly in the United States; no verified international operations.
rationale: Small listed company with a changing strategy and little brand awareness; limited fit for F1 sponsorship.
changed: Renamed from Thumzup Media

name: Cellecor
desc: Consumer electronics brand of Cellecor Gadgets Limited selling audio products, televisions, LED displays, smartwatches and home appliances in India.
markets: Retail and online customers in India; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Small Indian consumer-electronics brand listed on a small-company exchange; domestic focus and limited budget make F1 a weak fit.

name: Cosm
desc: Operates immersive Shared Reality venues with a large domed LED screen showing live sports, concerts and original content.
markets: Venues in Inglewood and the Dallas-Fort Worth area, with more United States cities planned.
rationale: Immersive-screen venues suit F1 watch parties, hospitality and technology showcase events, though footprint is US only.

name: Quantum Corporation
desc: Sells data storage and protection products including tape libraries, object storage, file systems and backup appliances.
markets: Enterprise, media and entertainment customers in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: B2B storage supplier serving video workflows could use F1 as a technology showcase, but consumer marketing is minimal.

name: TV Joy
desc: Described by Crunchbase as a children's animation and entertainment platform for large-screen devices, based in Nanjing.
markets: Audience presumed to be in China; no verified international operations.
rationale: Little-known Chinese children's content business with unclear scale; F1 offers weak audience fit.

name: NetEase Cloud Music
desc: Runs a Chinese online music streaming and social platform known for user comments, playlists and original music.
markets: Users in mainland China; no significant overseas operations.
rationale: Chinese music brand with young audience could add F1 playlist tie-ins in China, but it has no international footprint.

name: Douyu
desc: Operates a Chinese live-streaming platform focused on video games and esports, earning from virtual gifts, advertising and subscriptions.
markets: Viewers and streamers in China; no significant overseas operations.
rationale: Chinese gaming-stream platform with young male audience could pair with F1 esports content, but it is domestic and its status needs checking.

name: Kuaikan Manhua
desc: Runs a Chinese online comics platform offering original manhua on a free-and-paid model, backed by Tencent.
markets: Readers in China only; no verified overseas operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Chinese digital comics brand with a young audience; F1 tie-ins could be limited to character collaborations within China.

name: Litmus Music
desc: Music publishing and catalogue acquisition firm that buys and manages song rights from artists and writers.
markets: Catalogue acquisition from artists and writers, presumed mainly in the United States.
rationale: Investment-style rights buyer with no consumer brand; practical F1 sponsorship case is very weak.

name: Viu
desc: Video-on-demand streaming service offering Asian content, Korean dramas and local originals to subscribers across Asia and beyond.
markets: Subscribers in Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, the Middle East and South Africa.
rationale: Pan-Asian streamer with multi-market consumer marketing could use F1 audience tie-ins in Southeast Asia and the Gulf.

name: Devialet
desc: French luxury audio brand known for Phantom wireless speakers, the Dione soundbar and Gemini earbuds with patented amplifier technology.
markets: Premium audio products sold in Europe, North America and Asia through retail and online channels.
rationale: Premium audio brand with luxury positioning suits F1 hospitality, technology showcase and gifting, though scale is small.

name: Believe
desc: Provides digital music distribution and label services for independent artists and labels, including through TuneCore.
markets: Artists and labels in many countries across Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B music distributor with little consumer branding; F1 could offer artist-content tie-ins but fit is limited.
changed: Taken private in 2024 by a consortium including EQT and TCV

name: Gaana
desc: Music streaming app offering Bollywood, regional and international songs with free and paid tiers to users in India.
markets: Users in India only; no significant overseas operations or verified expansion plans.
rationale: Indian music app with consumer reach could use F1 playlist tie-ins in India, but its scale and budget are modest.

name: boAt
desc: Sells earbuds, headphones, speakers and smartwatches at affordable prices online and through retail, based in India.
markets: Customers mainly in India through online and retail channels; export plans not confirmed.
rationale: Youth-oriented Indian consumer brand with heavy sports marketing could use F1 as a growth showcase, though currently domestic.

name: QYOU Media
desc: Media company operating social and video content services, including content for Indian audiences, according to available data.
markets: Markets are not stated in the data; presumed North America.
rationale: Small listed media business with unclear current operations; limited fit for an F1 partnership.

name: China Unicom
desc: Provides mobile, broadband, fixed-line, cloud and data services to over 300 million mobile subscribers in China.
markets: Customers in mainland China, with some international network services; no expansion plans known.
rationale: Huge state-controlled operator with big marketing budgets, though customers are domestic and F1's Chinese Grand Prix is the only real tie-in.

name: Shanghai Canxing Cultural and Broadcast Company
desc: Described by Crunchbase as a Chinese media production firm that produces television programmes, based in Shanghai.
markets: Audience presumed to be in China; no international operations confirmed.
rationale: Little-known production firm with unclear scale, ownership and marketing activity, so F1 offers a weak partnership fit.

name: BAI Communications
desc: Owns and operates mobile, Wi-Fi and broadcast networks in transport systems and public venues for carriers and venue owners.
markets: Networks in Australia, the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada and Hong Kong.
rationale: Venue and transit connectivity operator could showcase stadium and event networks, though marketing is B2B and focused on infrastructure clients.

name: Quibi
desc: Was a short-form mobile video streaming service launched in 2020 by Jeffrey Katzenberg and Meg Whitman.
markets: Subscribers were in the United States and Canada; the service no longer operates.
rationale: Defunct service that shut down in 2020, so no partnership is possible with this brand.
changed: Shut down in December 2020; content library acquired by Roku in 2021

name: Kakao Entertainment
desc: Runs Korean webtoon and webnovel platforms including Piccoma, Tapas and Radish, music service Melon, and talent agencies.
markets: Content and platforms in South Korea, Japan, the United States and Southeast Asia.
rationale: Content group with global webtoon and K-pop audiences could do collaborations with F1 in Asia, but is not an established sports sponsor.

name: Cinemark
desc: Operates about 500 movie theaters and 5,700 screens in the United States and Latin America under Cinemark and Century brands.
markets: Moviegoers in the United States and Latin America; no confirmed expansion elsewhere.
rationale: Consumer cinema chain could screen F1 content and run promotions, though its footprint is limited to the Americas.

name: SM Entertainment
desc: Manages and produces K-pop artists such as aespa, NCT, Red Velvet and RIIZE, earning from music, concerts and merchandise.
markets: Fans across Asia, North America and Europe through tours, streaming and merchandise.
rationale: K-pop artist roster could add entertainment at Grand Prix weekends and Asian fan engagement, though it is not a typical sponsor.

name: Stingray
desc: Operates the Stingray Music streaming and broadcast service for businesses and consumers, plus karaoke and classical channels.
markets: Business and consumer customers in Canada, the United States, Europe and Latin America.
rationale: B2B music service with limited consumer brand; F1 tie-in possible for in-venue music, but marketing budget is modest.

name: Smarter Web Company
desc: Provides web design, hosting, compliance and content creation services to businesses and added bitcoin to its balance sheet.
markets: Business customers in the United Kingdom; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Small UK web-services business with limited brand awareness and modest scale; weak sponsorship fit.

name: Spotter
desc: Provides funding and services to online video creators, including buying rights to YouTube content libraries and advancing future earnings.
markets: Creators presumed mainly in the United States; international reach not confirmed.
rationale: Creator-finance firm with YouTube relationships could support F1 creator content, but it lacks brand marketing scale.

name: CuriosityStream
desc: Streams factual documentaries on science, nature and history, founded by Discovery Channel founder John Hendricks.
markets: Subscribers and licensing partners in the United States and other countries.
rationale: Niche documentary streamer could produce or distribute F1 content, but its marketing budget is small.

name: Synchronoss Technologies
desc: Provides cloud, messaging and digital experience platforms, including personal cloud storage white-labelled for mobile operators.
markets: Mobile operator customers in North America, Europe and other regions.
rationale: B2B software supplier to carriers with no consumer brand; F1 hospitality could help customer relationships, but fit is modest.

name: ADTRAN
desc: Makes broadband access, fiber, Wi-Fi and optical networking equipment and software for telecom operators and enterprises.
markets: Operators and enterprises across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B network supplier could use F1 for customer hospitality and a technology showcase, as rival network suppliers already do.

name: Substack
desc: Runs a subscription newsletter platform where writers, journalists and podcasters send paid newsletters and build audiences.
markets: Writers and readers worldwide, mainly English-speaking markets led by the United States.
rationale: Creator platform with sophisticated audience but few brand-marketing partnerships; F1 content collaboration possible but sponsorship fit is weak.

name: Animaj
desc: Creates animated children's series and uses AI in production, with brands including Pocoyo, Treehouse Detectives and Wondermoms.
markets: Children's content reaching audiences in Europe, the Americas and Asia through YouTube and streaming.
rationale: Children's animation owner with global audience could pursue licensing collaborations, but F1 audience fit is limited.

name: Corus Entertainment
desc: Owns Canadian specialty television channels such as Global TV, W Network and Treehouse, radio stations and children's producer Nelvana.
markets: Audiences and advertisers in Canada; Nelvana content is licensed internationally.
rationale: Canadian broadcaster with advertiser-led revenue could support F1 Canadian Grand Prix promotions, but is a domestic media group.

name: Amaze Software
desc: Provides a creator commerce platform helping creators and brands build online stores, link pages and sell products to audiences.
markets: Creators and brands presumed mainly in the United States; international reach not confirmed.
rationale: Small creator-commerce software company with limited brand awareness; weak F1 fit beyond merchandise-store ideas.

name: Unrivaled
desc: Professional women's 3-on-3 basketball league founded by WNBA stars Breanna Stewart and Napheesa Collier, first played in 2025.
markets: Games and fans in the United States; no verified international plans.
rationale: Young US women's league that could pair with F1 Academy audience themes, but it is domestic and early-stage.

name: Miaopai
desc: Short-video sharing and live streaming app launched in 2014 with backing from Sina Weibo and Tencent.
markets: Users in China only; no verified overseas operations or expansion plans known.
rationale: Chinese short-video app with an unclear current operating status and a domestic audience; weak case for an F1 partnership.

name: SoundCloud
desc: Runs an audio streaming platform where artists upload music and podcasts and listeners stream free or by subscription.
markets: Artists and listeners worldwide across Europe, North America and Asia.
rationale: Artist-led music platform with young audience could host F1 content and artist collaborations, though sponsor budget is modest.

name: Guitar Center
desc: United States retailer of musical instruments with about 300 stores selling guitars, drums, keyboards and DJ gear.
markets: Stores and online customers in the United States only.
rationale: US instrument retailer with consumer marketing could do music-themed F1 events, though it has no international footprint.
changed: Restructured under Chapter 11 in 2020

name: Harmonic
desc: Sells video processing and delivery software, the VOS360 cloud streaming platform and cable broadband access equipment to service providers.
markets: Service providers and broadcasters across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B video-technology supplier could use F1 as a showcase for live streaming technology and customer hospitality.

name: Beckett Collectibles
desc: Publishes price guides for sports cards and collectibles, runs Beckett Grading Services and operates an online marketplace.
markets: Collectors presumed mainly in the United States; wider reach not confirmed.
rationale: Trading-card grading brand with collector audience could link to F1 card and memorabilia collecting, though sponsorship scale is small.

name: Wavve
desc: Korean streaming service formed in 2019 from broadcaster app Pooq and SK Telecom's Oksusu, offering video on demand.
markets: Subscribers in South Korea; no verified international operations.
rationale: Domestic Korean streamer with broadcaster owners; limited reach beyond Korea gives weak F1 fit.

name: Anghami
desc: Music streaming platform for the Arab world with over 100 million songs, podcasts and original Arabic content.
markets: Subscribers across the Middle East and North Africa, with operations based in Abu Dhabi.
rationale: Gulf consumer brand with regional music audience could tie in with Abu Dhabi, Qatar and Saudi Grand Prix weekends.
changed: Majority stake acquired by OSN Streaming in 2024

name: Bang & Olufsen
desc: Makes premium televisions, loudspeakers, headphones and home audio systems with high-end design, sold under the Beosound and Beovision names.
industry: luxury consumer audio and television maker
markets: Customers across Europe, the Americas and Asia through own stores and retailers.
rationale: Luxury brand with global distribution suits F1 hospitality, paddock gifting and brand-association marketing.

name: Automattic
desc: Software company behind WordPress.com, WooCommerce, Jetpack, Tumblr, Simplenote and Day One, earning from subscriptions, hosting and commerce plug-ins.
markets: Customers worldwide across web publishing and commerce, with a distributed workforce rather than a single headquarters.
rationale: Developer-focused web brand could use F1 for technology showcase and customer events, but has little history of sports sponsorship.

name: Cenveo
desc: Was a commercial printing and marketing communications firm making envelopes, labels, forms, custom packaging and printed marketing materials.
markets: Corporate, publishing and financial customers mainly in the United States; no longer operating as before.
rationale: Defunct printer that went bankrupt in 2018 with no ongoing brand, so no partnership is possible.
changed: Filed for Chapter 11 in 2018 and its operating businesses were sold

name: Huya
desc: Operates a Chinese game live-streaming platform where viewers watch esports and gameplay and tip streamers, spun out of YY.
markets: Viewers and streamers in China; no significant overseas operations.
rationale: Chinese gaming-stream brand with young audience could add F1 esports content, but its reach is domestic.

name: Coda
desc: Digital payments and commerce company behind Codashop and Coda Payments, letting gamers buy in-game currency and top up mobile games.
markets: Gamers in Southeast Asia and other regions, with local payment methods across many countries.
rationale: Gaming-payments brand with marketing to young gamers could use F1 for brand visibility in Asia and emerging markets.

name: Improbable
desc: Built SpatialOS cloud simulation technology and pursues virtual worlds and games, including MSquared, after selling its defence business.
markets: Customers include game studios, governments and enterprises; operations centred in London.
rationale: Technology firm with simulation expertise could use F1 as a technology showcase, but it lacks consumer marketing scale.
changed: Sold its defence business to Bohemia Interactive Simulations in 2022

name: Opry
desc: Described by Crunchbase as an online platform offering independent artists tools to reach audiences, tagged with art and media.
markets: Markets not stated in the data; presumed United States only.
rationale: Name may be misread and the company is unclear; no evidence of marketing capacity for an F1 partnership.

name: Keywords Studios
desc: Supports video game developers with art, audio and voice recording, localisation, quality assurance and player support.
markets: Game publishers and developers worldwide through studios in dozens of countries.
rationale: B2B services provider to game studios with little consumer branding; F1 gaming tie-ins could support client relationships.
changed: Taken private in 2024 by EQT

name: Cogeco Communications
desc: Provides internet, television and phone services to homes and businesses in Quebec and Ontario and in the United States.
markets: Customers in Quebec, Ontario and the United States; no further expansion known.
rationale: Regional cable operator with Canadian Grand Prix in its home province, but limited scale and a utility-style brand.

name: Vox Media
desc: Owns digital media brands Vox, The Verge, Eater, Polygon, SB Nation and New York Magazine, plus podcast and video businesses.
markets: Audiences and advertisers mainly in the United States; no confirmed overseas expansion.
rationale: Digital publisher with advertising sales could produce F1 content and host sponsor events, but audience is mainly American.

name: Zee Entertainment Enterprises
desc: Operates Zee TV, Zee Cinema and Zee News channels and the Zee5 streaming service, reaching viewers in India and abroad.
markets: Viewers across India and Indian diaspora markets in North America, Europe, the Middle East and Africa.
rationale: Large Indian broadcaster with diaspora reach could use F1 to promote its programming and advertising inventory.
changed: Merger with Sony Pictures Networks India was called off in 2024

name: Grass Valley
desc: Makes broadcast and live production technology including video switchers, cameras, servers and the AMPP cloud production platform.
markets: Broadcasters, sports producers and media companies worldwide; no specific expansion plans known to me.
rationale: B2B broadcast technology supplier could use F1 as a showcase for live production technology and customer hospitality.
changed: Sold by Belden to Black Dragon Capital in 2020

name: Regal
desc: Operates a United States movie theatre chain with several hundred cinemas, owned by Cineworld.
markets: Moviegoers in the United States only; no international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Cinema chain could host F1 screenings, but its owner has been through bankruptcy and the footprint is domestic.
changed: Parent Cineworld filed for Chapter 11 in 2022 and emerged in 2023

name: Lionsgate Studios
desc: Film and television studio behind The Hunger Games, John Wick, Saw and Twilight, earning from releases and streaming licences.
markets: Films and television licensed to audiences across North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Studio with franchise brands suits content tie-ins and premieres around F1 events, though it is not a regular sports sponsor.
changed: Separated from Starz in 2025 and listed as Lionsgate Studios

name: Brazil Tower Company
desc: Builds, owns and leases telecom towers and rooftop sites to mobile operators in Brazil.
markets: Mobile carrier customers in Brazil only; no international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: B2B infrastructure business with no consumer brand; F1 relevance limited to occasional Brazilian Grand Prix hospitality.

name: Juventus
desc: Italian football club in Turin with a record number of Serie A titles, earning from matchdays, media rights and sponsorship.
markets: Fans and commercial partners across Europe, Asia and the Americas.
rationale: Global football brand with large international fan base and corporate hospitality suits cross-promotion with F1 in Italy and abroad.

name: Kinepolis Group
desc: Operates large multiplex cinemas in Belgium, France, Spain, the Netherlands, Luxembourg, Switzerland, Canada and the United States.
markets: Cinemas in several European countries plus Canada and the United States.
rationale: Cinema chain could screen F1 races and run hospitality events, though marketing budget is modest and customers are casual.

name: Lingokids
desc: Sells a subscription app teaching English and other skills to children aged 2 to 8 through games, songs and videos.
markets: Families in the United States, Latin America and Spain.
rationale: Family edtech brand could pair with F1 youth education themes, but its audience is young children and its budget small.

name: Electric Entertainment
desc: Film, television and digital production company founded by Dean Devlin, behind Leverage, The Librarians and Geostorm.
markets: Production for United States studios and networks and international buyers.
rationale: Small independent producer with no consumer brand; F1 content collaboration possible but fit is weak.

name: TeraDAR
desc: Develops terahertz-based sensors for vehicles combining the strengths of radar and lidar, aimed at automated driving and robotics.
markets: Early-stage and pre-revenue; targets automakers and suppliers, with operations in the United States.
rationale: Pre-revenue deep-tech sensor developer with no consumer brand; any F1 contact would be technology-showcase only.
